Sergio Aragonés Drawn-Out Dramas


A chronological list of his marginals in MAD Magazine


sorted by regular issue as they were compiled
For nearly sixty years Sergio Aragonés produced little drawings to fill the margins
in the pages of MAD Magazine beginning with issue #76, January 1963.
Thousands of examples later, a few lost souls tried to organize it all!
Welcome to the project page!
This is a record of the collaborative effort a group of us went through and never finished.
The following was a list of my "directions" to those who wanted to be involved before I burned out on it:

"Looking forward to collaborating with you.
If you'd like to be involved let me know through email (madcoversite@yahoo.com).

Do one issue. Do one hundred issues. Whatever you want to do. Complete issues only.
Put together a list like the examples below and email me, preferably in a spreadsheet format, but whatever works for you.
I'll put your name below the issue list as the compiler for any issues you want to take responsibility for.

There is no real order to this. As I get an issue, I'll insert it where it belongs in the chronological flow of things.
Brevity in descriptions is a plus, but detail wins in the end for future searches (CTRL-F).
When possible, try to describe things happening in the present tense.
I will edit for clarity and I invite others to offer better descriptions if they have them.
The page orientation descriptions should be simple. Don't worry about being too exact here.
Use the word "side" when the marginal runs vertically on a page side, otherwise we'll assume it runs horizonally.
Use the word "vertical" in cases when it's not placed on a page side (happened a lot within The Lighter Side of...).
In later issues, Sergio did a lot of "spot" illustrations in the contents and letters pages.
These weren't necessarily "marginals" in the truest sense. Their inclusion will be determined on an issue by issue basis.

Each issue page will have a link to the corresponding entry on this list!"
